title.zh: 卷八十五 列傳第二十三: 世宗諸子 永中 永蹈 永功子:璹(本名壽孫) 永德 永成 永升
title.en: Volume 85 Biographies 23: Sons of Shizong: Yong Zhong, Yong Dao, Yong Gong Son: Shu (Former Name Shousun), Yong De, Yong Cheng, Yong Sheng
title.raw: 卷八十五 列傳第二十三: 世宗諸子 永中 永蹈 永功子:璹(本名壽孫) 永德 永成 永升 Volume 85 Biographies 23: Sons of Shizong: Yong Zhong, Yong Dao, Yong Gong Son: Shu (Former Name Shousun), Yong De, Yong Cheng, Yong Sheng

sentences.zh: 世宗昭德皇后生顯宗、趙王孰輦、越王斜魯。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaode of Shizong bore Xianzong, Prince of Zhao Shunian, and Prince of Yue Xielu.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's Empress Zhaode gave birth to Xianzong, to Shunian, Prince of Zhao, and to Xielu, Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 元妃張氏生鄗王允中、越王允功。

translations.literal: Primary consort Zhang bore Prince of Hao Yun Zhong and Prince of Yue Yun Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The primary consort, Lady Zhang, bore Yun Zhong, Prince of Hao, and Yun Gong, Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 元妃李氏生鄭王允蹈、衛紹王允濟、潞王允德。

translations.literal: Primary consort Li bore Prince of Zheng Yun Dao, Prince of Wei-Shao Yun Ji, and Prince of Lu Yun De.
translations.idiomatic: The primary consort, Lady Li, bore Yun Dao, Prince of Zheng; Yun Ji, Prince of Wei-Shao; and Yun De, Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 昭儀梁氏生豫王允成。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi Liang bore Prince of Yu Yun Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liang, a zhaoyi, bore Yun Cheng, Prince of Yu.

sentences.zh: 才人石抹氏生夔王允升。

translations.literal: Talented Lady Shimozhi bore Prince of Kui Yun Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The talented lady Shimozhi bore Yun Sheng, Prince of Kui.

sentences.zh: 孰輦、斜魯皆早卒。

translations.literal: Shunian and Xielu both died early.
translations.idiomatic: Shunian and Xielu both died in youth.

sentences.zh: 鎬王永中，本名實魯剌，又名萬僧。

translations.literal: Prince of Hao Yong Zhong, original name Shilula, was also called Wanseng.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Zhong, Prince of Hao, born Shilula, was also known as Wanseng.

sentences.zh: 大定元年，封許王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dading he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dading he was made Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 五年，判大興尹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Administrator of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Administrator of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 七年，進封越王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was advanced to Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進封趙王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was advanced to Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 十三年，拜樞密使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十九年，子石古乃加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year his son Shigu Nai was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year his son Shigu Nai was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 是歲，改葬明德皇后于坤厚陵，永中母元妃張氏陪葬。

translations.literal: That year Empress Mingde was reinterred at Kunhou Tomb, and Yong Zhong's mother, primary consort Lady Zhang, was buried with her.
translations.idiomatic: That year Empress Mingde was reinterred at Kunhou Tomb, and Yong Zhong's mother, the primary consort Lady Zhang, was buried with her.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚申，自磐甯宮發引。

translations.literal: On gengshen day in the eleventh month the funeral procession set out from Panning Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the eleventh month the funeral procession set out from Panning Palace.

sentences.zh: 永中以元妃柩先發，使執黃傘者前導。

translations.literal: Yong Zhong had the primary consort's bier set out first and ordered men bearing yellow canopies to go ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Zhong sent the primary consort's bier out first and had men with yellow canopies go ahead as guides.

sentences.zh: 俄頃，皇后柩出磐甯宮，顯宗徒跣。

translations.literal: Before long the empress's bier came out of Panning Palace, and Xianzong went barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the empress's bier emerged from Panning Palace, and Xianzong went barefoot.

sentences.zh: 少府監張僅言呼執黃傘者，不應。

translations.literal: Junior Palace Steward Zhang Jinyan called to the canopy-bearers, but they did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Palace Steward Zhang Jinyan called to the canopy-bearers, but they did not respond.

sentences.zh: 既葬，僅言欲奏其事，顯宗解之曰：「是何足校哉，或傘人誤耳。」

translations.literal: After the burial Jinyan wished to memorialize the matter, but Xianzong explained it, saying: "What is there worth disputing? Perhaps the canopy-bearers made a mistake."
translations.idiomatic: After the burial Jinyan wanted to report the matter, but Xianzong dismissed it, saying: "What is there worth disputing? Perhaps the canopy-bearers simply made a mistake."

sentences.zh: 僅言乃止。

translations.literal: Jinyan then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyan then let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，改判大宗正事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, [his appointment] was changed to director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was reassigned to head the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 永中不悅，顯宗勸之曰：「宗正之職，自親及疏，自近及遠，此親賢之任也。

translations.literal: Yong Zhong was displeased. Xianzong urged him, saying: "The duty of the Imperial Clan Court extends from the close to the distant, from the near to the far — this is the charge of cherishing worthy kin.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Zhong took offense, but Xianzong persuaded him: "The Imperial Clan Court's charge runs from the nearest kin outward to the most distant — it is the task of honoring the worthy among one's relatives.

sentences.zh: 且皇子之貴，豈以官職閑劇為計邪？」

translations.literal: Moreover, can a prince's dignity be measured by whether an office is prestigious or menial?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, is a prince's standing really to be reckoned by how grand or humble his post may be?"

sentences.zh: 永中乃喜。

translations.literal: Yong Zhong was then pleased.
translations.idiomatic: With that, Yong Zhong was satisfied.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，世宗幸上京，顯宗居守，並留永中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Shizong visited the Upper Capital. Xianzong remained to guard [the capital], and Yong Zhong was also left behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Shizong went to the Upper Capital; Xianzong stayed behind to guard the realm, and Yong Zhong was left behind as well.

sentences.zh: 顯宗先遣章宗、宣宗奉表問起居於上京，既而遣永中子光祿大夫石古乃奉表。

translations.literal: Xianzong first sent Zhangzong and Xuanzong to present memorials inquiring after Shizong's health at the Upper Capital; afterward he sent Yong Zhong's son, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Shigu Nai, to present a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong first dispatched Zhangzong and Xuanzong to the Upper Capital with memorials inquiring after the emperor's health; he then sent Yong Zhong's son Shigu Nai, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with another memorial.

sentences.zh: 世宗喜謂豫國公主曰：「皇太子孝德天成，先遣二子，繼遣此子，兄弟之際相友愛如此也。」

translations.literal: Shizong said with pleasure to the Princess of Yu State: "The Heir Apparent's filial virtue is innate. He first sent his two sons, then sent this son — such mutual affection between brothers!"
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Shizong told the Princess of Yu: "The crown prince's filial devotion is inborn. He sent his two sons first, then this son — such brotherly affection as this!"

sentences.zh: 二十五年六月，世宗在天平山好水川清暑，顯宗薨於中都，詔曹王永功視章宗，召永中赴行在。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year, while Shizong was taking the cool air at Haoshuichuan on Tianping Mountain, Xianzong died in the Central Capital. An edict ordered Prince of Cao Yong Gong to attend Zhangzong and summoned Yong Zhong to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-fifth year, while Shizong was summering at Haoshuichuan on Tianping Mountain, Xianzong died in the Central Capital. An edict ordered Prince Cao Yong Gong to look after Zhangzong and summoned Yong Zhong to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 是歲，與章宗及永功等並加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: That year he, Zhangzong, Yong Gong, and the others were all granted the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: That year he, Zhangzong, Yong Gong, and the others were all given the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，複為樞密使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was again made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was again made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是歲，世宗賜諸孫名。

translations.literal: That year Shizong granted names to his grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shizong gave names to his grandsons.

sentences.zh: 石古乃曰瑜，神土門日璋，阿思懣曰槩，阿離合懣曰曁彖。

translations.literal: Shigu Nai was named Yu, Shentumen was named Zhang, Asimen was named Gai, and Alihemen was named Jitan.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu Nai was named Yu, Shentumen was named Zhang, Asimen was named Gai, and Alihemen was named Jitan.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，槩年十五以上，加奉國上將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Gai, being fifteen or older, was promoted to General-in-Chief Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Gai, then fifteen or older, was made General-in-Chief Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，起複判西京留守，進封漢王，與諸弟各賜金五百兩、銀五千兩、錢二千貫、重幣三百端、絹二千匹。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, Yong Zhong was recalled and appointed to serve as Western Capital regent, advanced to Prince of Han, and each of the princes was granted five hundred taels of gold, five thousand taels of silver, two thousand strings of cash, three hundred bolts of heavy silks, and two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong came to the throne, Yong Zhong was recalled to serve as regent of the Western Capital and promoted to Prince of Han. Each of the princes received five hundred taels of gold, five thousand taels of silver, two thousand strings of cash, three hundred bolts of heavy silks, and two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 再賜永中修公廨錢三百萬，特加石古乃銀青榮祿大夫，阿離合懣奉國上將軍。

translations.literal: Yong Zhong was further granted three million in cash to repair his official residence; Shigu Nai was specially made Silver-Green Glory Grandee, and Alihemen was made General-in-Chief Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Zhong was further given three million in cash to repair his official residence; Shigu Nai was specially made Silver-Green Glory Grandee, and Alihemen was made General-in-Chief Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年正月辛酉，孝懿皇后崩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Mingchang, on the xinyou day, Empress Xiaoyi died.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day of the first month in the second year of Mingchang, Empress Xiaoyi passed away.

sentences.zh: 判真定府事吳王永成、判定武軍節度使隋王永升奔喪後期，各罰俸一月，杖其長史五十。

translations.literal: Wu Wang Yongcheng, administering Zhending Prefecture, and Sui Wang Yongsheng, military commissioner of Dingwu Army, arrived late for the mourning; each was fined one month's salary, and their chief administrators were beaten fifty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wu Yongcheng, who was administering Zhending, and Prince Sui Yongsheng, commissioner of the Dingwu army, came late to the mourning. Each was docked a month's pay, and their chief administrators were flogged fifty times.

sentences.zh: 永中適有寒疾，不能至。

translations.literal: Yong Zhong happened to have a cold and could not come.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Zhong was laid up with a chill and could not attend.

sentences.zh: 上怒，頗意諸王有輕慢心，遣使責永中曰：「已近公除，亦不須來。」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and suspected the princes of harboring disrespect. He sent a messenger to reprove Yong Zhong, saying: "The public mourning period is nearly over; you need not come at all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and came to suspect the princes of contempt. He sent someone to rebuke Yong Zhong: "The mourning period is almost finished — you need not come at all."

sentences.zh: 二月丙戌，禫祭，永中始至，入臨。

translations.literal: On bingxu day in the second month, at the end-of-mourning sacrifice, Yong Zhong arrived at last and went in to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu in the second month, at the final mourning rites, Yong Zhong arrived at last and went in to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，始克行燒飯禮。

translations.literal: On xinmao day, he was finally able to perform the burnt-offering rite.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he was at last able to carry out the burnt-offering ceremony.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，永中及諸王朝辭，賜遺留物，禮遇雖在，而嫌忌自此始矣。

translations.literal: On renchen day, Yong Zhong and the other princes took leave of the court. They were granted parting gifts; though courtesies remained, suspicion began from this point.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Yong Zhong and the other princes took their leave of court and were given parting gifts. The forms of honor were still observed, but distrust began from that moment.

sentences.zh: 四月，進封並王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, [he] was advanced to Prince of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was promoted to Prince of Bing.

sentences.zh: 三年，判平陽府事，進封鎬王。

translations.literal: In the third year, [he] was appointed to administer Pingyang Prefecture and advanced to Prince of Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was put in charge of Pingyang Prefecture and raised to Prince of Hao.

sentences.zh: 初置王傅、府尉官，名為官屬，實檢制之也。

translations.literal: Tutor and prefectural marshal posts for princes were first established — nominally staff, but in fact to keep them under surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: Tutors and prefectural marshals for princes were instituted for the first time: in name they were household staff, but in practice they were there to restrain them.

sentences.zh: 府尉希望風旨，過為苛細。

translations.literal: The prefectural marshals, eager to read the court's intentions, were excessively harsh in petty matters.
translations.idiomatic: The marshals, straining to divine the court's wishes, went to petty extremes.

sentences.zh: 永中自以世宗長子，且老矣，動有掣制，情思不堪，殊鬱鬱，乃表乞閒居。

translations.literal: Yong Zhong considered himself Shizong's eldest son and, now old, found himself checked at every turn; his spirits could not bear it. Utterly depressed, he memorialized begging to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Zhong regarded himself as Shizong's eldest son and, now advanced in years, felt thwarted at every turn until he could endure it no longer. Deeply dispirited, he submitted a memorial asking to live in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 詔不許。

translations.literal: An edict refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 四年，鄭王永蹈以謀逆誅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Prince of Zheng Yong Dao was executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Prince Zheng Yong Dao was put to death for treason.

sentences.zh: 增置諸王司馬一員，檢察門戶出入，球獵遊宴皆有制限，家人出入皆有禁防。

translations.literal: One additional Chief Clerk for Princes was added to inspect household comings and goings; ball games, hunting, and banquets were all subject to limits, and family members' movements were restricted.
translations.idiomatic: An extra chief clerk for princes was appointed to watch over comings and goings at their gates; ball games, hunting, and feasting were all curtailed, and even their households were barred from moving freely.

sentences.zh: 河東提刑判官把里海坐私謁永中，杖一百，解職。

translations.literal: Ba Li Hai, investigating commissioner of Hedong, was sentenced to one hundred strokes for paying a private visit to Yong Zhong, and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Ba Li Hai, the investigating commissioner in Hedong, was flogged a hundred times and removed from office for visiting Yong Zhong in private.

sentences.zh: 前近侍局副使裴滿可孫嘗受永中請托，為石古乃求除官，可孫已改同知西京留守，猶坐免。

translations.literal: Former Vice Commissioner of the Inner Service Bureau Peiman Kesun had once accepted Yong Zhong's request and sought an appointment for Shigu Nai; though Kesun had already been transferred to be co-administrator of the Western Capital's garrison, he was still dismissed for this.
translations.idiomatic: Peiman Kesun, formerly vice commissioner of the Inner Service Bureau, had once taken Yong Zhong's commission and lobbied for an appointment for Shigu Nai. Though Kesun had already been made co-administrator of the Western Capital garrison, he was still stripped of his post on that account.

sentences.zh: 故尚書右丞張汝弼，永中母舅也。

translations.literal: Former Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhang Rubi was Yong Zhong's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: The late Right Vice Director Zhang Rubi was Yong Zhong's uncle on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 汝弼妻高陀斡自大定間畫永中母像，奉之甚謹，挾左道為永中求福，希覬非望。

translations.literal: Rubi's wife Gaotuowo had painted a portrait of Yong Zhong's mother since the Dading period and worshipped it with great care; she employed heterodox arts to seek blessings for Yong Zhong and cherished unlawful ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi's wife Gaotuowo had painted a portrait of Yong Zhong's mother as far back as the Dading era and tended it with scrupulous devotion; she turned to unorthodox rites to win blessings for Yong Zhong and harbored forbidden hopes.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年，高陀斡坐詛祝誅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang, Gaotuowo was executed for cursing and sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Mingchang Gaotuowo was executed for curse-magic and imprecation.

sentences.zh: 上疑事在永中，未有以發也。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected the matter involved Yong Zhong but had no grounds to act.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected Yong Zhong was implicated, but had no occasion to move against him.

sentences.zh: 會鎬王傅尉奏永中第四子阿離合懣因防禁嚴密，語涉不道。

translations.literal: At this time the tutor and marshal of the Prince of Hao reported that Yong Zhong's fourth son Alikemian, because the restrictions were severe, had spoken words bordering on treason.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Prince of Hao's tutor and marshal reported that Yong Zhong's fourth son Alikemian, chafing under the tight restrictions, had uttered words that smacked of sedition.

sentences.zh: 詔同簽大睦親府事袴、禦史中丞孫即康鞫問，並求得第二子神徒門所撰詞曲有不遜語。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Co-signatory of the Imperial Clan Court Affairs Ku and Censor-in-Chief Sun Jikang to interrogate him; they also obtained song lyrics written by the second son Shentumen containing disrespectful language.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Ku, co-signatory of the Imperial Clan Court, and Censor-in-Chief Sun Jikang to question him, and they also recovered song lyrics by his second son Shentumen that contained irreverent lines.

sentences.zh: 家奴德哥首永中嘗與侍妾瑞雪言：「我得天下，子為大王，以爾為妃。」

translations.literal: The household slave Degé accused that Yong Zhong had once said to his concubine Ruixue: "When I obtain the realm, my son shall be a great prince, and you shall be consort."
translations.idiomatic: A household slave named Degé reported that Yong Zhong had once told his concubine Ruixue: "When I win the realm, my son will be a great prince and you shall be my consort."

sentences.zh: 詔遣官複按狀同。

translations.literal: An edict sent officials to reinvestigate; the case matched.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were sent to reinvestigate, and the account was confirmed.

sentences.zh: 再遣禮部尚書張暐、兵部侍郎烏古論慶裔複之。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei, Minister of Rites, and Wugulun Qingyi, Vice Minister of War, were sent to investigate again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei of the Ministry of Rites and Wugulun Qingyi, vice minister of war, were dispatched to examine the matter once more.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰臣曰：「鎬王只以語言得罪，與永蹈罪異。」

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers: "The Prince of Hao is guilty only of words, which is different from Yong Dao's crime."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers: "The Prince of Hao has offended only in speech — his case is not the same as Yong Dao's."

sentences.zh: 參知政事馬琪曰：「永中與永蹈罪狀雖異，人臣無將，則一也。」

translations.literal: Vice Director Ma Qi said: "Though Yong Zhong's and Yong Dao's offenses differ in form, in a subject's presumption of rule there is no difference."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Ma Qi replied: "Yong Zhong's and Yong Dao's crimes may look different, but in the presumption of a subject to rule, they are one and the same."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「大王何故輒出此言？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Great Prince, why do you speak so rashly?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Great Prince, why do you blurt out such words?"

sentences.zh: 左丞相清臣曰：「素有妄想之心也。」

translations.literal: Left Director Qingchen said: "He has long harbored deluded ambition."
translations.idiomatic: Left Director Qingchen said: "He has long nursed delusions of power."

sentences.zh: 詔以永中罪狀宣示百官雜議，五品以下附奏，四品以上入對便殿。

translations.literal: An edict directed that Yong Zhong's crimes be proclaimed to the officials for joint deliberation; fifth rank and below submitted attached memorials, fourth rank and above entered the side hall to respond.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Yong Zhong's crimes known to the officials for joint deliberation: those of fifth rank and below submitted attached memorials, while those of fourth rank and above were received in the side hall.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「請論如律。」

translations.literal: All said: "We ask that judgment follow the law."
translations.idiomatic: All said: "We ask that he be judged according to law."

sentences.zh: 惟宮籍監丞盧利用乞貸其死。

translations.literal: Only Palace Register Supervisor Assistant Lu Liyong begged that his life be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lu Liyong, assistant supervisor of the palace register, pleaded that his life be spared.

sentences.zh: 詔賜永中死，神徒門、阿離合懣等皆棄市。

translations.literal: An edict granted Yong Zhong death by suicide; Shentumen, Alikemian, and others were all executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed Yong Zhong to take his own life; Shentumen, Alikemian, and the rest were executed in public.

sentences.zh: 敕有司用國公禮收葬永中，平陽府監護，官給葬具，妻子威州安置。

translations.literal: An order directed the authorities to bury Yong Zhong with the rites due a state duke, with Pingyang Prefecture supervising; funeral goods were supplied by the state, and his wife and children were settled at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities were ordered to bury Yong Zhong with the rites of a state duke under Pingyang's supervision, with state-provided funeral goods, while his wife and children were resettled at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 泰和七年，詔複永中王爵，賜諡曰厲。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe, an edict restored Yong Zhong's princely rank and granted the posthumous name Li.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taihe an edict restored Yong Zhong's princely title and gave him the posthumous name Li.

sentences.zh: 敕石古乃於威州擇地，以禮改葬，歲時祭奠。

translations.literal: Shigu Nai was ordered to choose a site at Weizhou for reburial according to ritual, with seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu Nai was ordered to choose a site at Weizhou and rebury him according to ritual, with sacrifices at the proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，詔徙永中妻、子石古乃等鄭州安置。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, an edict moved Yong Zhong's wife and son Shigu Nai and others to Zhengzhou for resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou an edict relocated Yong Zhong's wife, his son Shigu Nai, and the rest to Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年，太康縣人劉全嘗為盜，亡入衛真界，詭稱愛王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou, Liu Quan of Taikang County, who had once been a bandit, fled into the Weizhen region and falsely claimed to be the Beloved Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyou Liu Quan of Taikang County, a former bandit, fled into the Weizhen district and passed himself off as the Beloved Prince.

sentences.zh: 所謂愛王，指石古乃。

translations.literal: The so-called Beloved Prince referred to Shigu Nai.
translations.idiomatic: The "Beloved Prince" in question was Shigu Nai.

sentences.zh: 石古乃實未嘗有王封，小人妄以此目之。

translations.literal: Shigu Nai had in fact never held a princely title; common people had recklessly applied this label to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu Nai had never in fact held a princely title; petty men had invented the name for him.

sentences.zh: 劉全欲為亂，因假託以惑眾，誘王氏女為妻，且言其子方聚兵河北。

translations.literal: Liu Quan wished to raise rebellion and used this false pretense to delude the crowd; he enticed a Wang clanswoman to be his wife and also claimed that his son was gathering troops in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan meant to stir up trouble and used the imposture to mislead the people; he lured a Wang clanswoman into marriage and claimed that his son was raising an army in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 東平人李甯居嵩山，有妖術。

translations.literal: Li Ning of Dongping lived on Mount Song and possessed sorcerous arts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ning of Dongping lived on Mount Song and practiced occult arts.

sentences.zh: 全同縣人時溫稱寧可論大事，乃使範元書偽號召之。

translations.literal: Shi Wen of the same county said that Ning could discuss great affairs, and so had Fan Yuan write a forged summons in the imperial style to call him.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow townsman named Shi Wen said Ning was fit to counsel on great matters, and had Fan Yuan draft a forged imperial summons to bring him.

sentences.zh: 甯至，推為國師，議僭立。

translations.literal: When Ning arrived, [they] made him National Preceptor and discussed usurping the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Ning arrived they proclaimed him National Preceptor and debated setting up a rival ruler.

sentences.zh: 事覺，全、溫、寧皆伏誅。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, Quan, Wen, and Ning were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot came to light, Quan, Wen, and Ning were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 貞祐四年，潼關破，徙永中子孫于南京。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyou, Tong Pass fell, and Yong Zhong's descendants were moved to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenyou, after Tong Pass fell, Yong Zhong's descendants were relocated to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 興定二年，亳州譙縣人孫學究私造妖言雲：「愛王終當奮發，今匿跡民間，自號劉二。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingding, Sun Xuejiu of Qiao County in Bozhou privately fabricated demonic talk, saying: "The Beloved Prince will surely rise in the end; he now hides among the people and calls himself Liu the Second."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xingding Sun Xuejiu of Qiao County in Bozhou spread seditious prophecy: "The Beloved Prince will surely rise at last; he now hides among the common people and styles himself Liu the Second."

sentences.zh: 衛真百姓王深等皆信以為誠然。

translations.literal: The commoners Wang Shen and others of Weizhen all believed this to be true.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen and other commoners of Weizhen took it all for truth.

sentences.zh: 有劉二者出而當之，遣歐榮輩結構逆黨，市兵仗，大署旌旗，謀慄立。

translations.literal: A certain Liu the Second came forward to fill the role; he sent Ou Rong and his kind to form a rebel faction, bought weapons, raised banners on a grand scale, and plotted usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: A man calling himself Liu the Second stepped forward to play the part; he sent Ou Rong and others to knit together a rebel band, bought arms, unfurled great banners, and plotted to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 事覺，誅死者五十二人，緣坐者六十餘人。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, fifty-two were executed and more than sixty were implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, fifty-two were put to death and more than sixty were punished as accomplices.

sentences.zh: 永中子孫禁錮，自明昌至於正大末，幾四十年。

translations.literal: Yong Zhong's descendants were confined; from Mingchang to the end of Zhengda, it was nearly forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Zhong's line was kept under confinement from Mingchang down to the end of Zhengda — nearly forty years in all.

sentences.zh: 天興初，詔弛禁錮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing, an edict relaxed the confinement.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianxing an edict lifted the restrictions.

sentences.zh: 未幾，南京亦不守雲。

translations.literal: Before long, Nanjing too was no longer held.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Nanjing too was lost.

sentences.zh: 鄭王永蹈，本名銀術可，初名石狗兒。

translations.literal: Prince of Zheng Yong Dao, original name Yinshuke, was first named Shigou'er.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Dao, Prince of Zheng, born Yinshuke, was originally named Shigou'er.

sentences.zh: 大定十一年，封滕王，未期月進封徐王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dading he was enfeoffed as Prince of Teng; before a month had passed he was advanced to Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Dading he was made Prince of Teng, and within a month was promoted to Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was granted the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was given the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，為大興尹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he became Administrator of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was made Administrator of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，判彰德軍節度使，進封衛王。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, Yong Dao was appointed military commissioner of Zhangde Army and advanced to Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong came to the throne, Yong Dao was made commissioner of the Zhangde army and promoted to Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，徙封鄭王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingchang he was transferred to Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingchang he was reassigned as Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，改判定武軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to administer the Dingwu army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was reassigned to administer the Dingwu army.

sentences.zh: 初，崔溫、郭諫、馬太初與永蹈家奴畢慶壽私說讖記災祥，畢慶壽以告永蹈：「郭諫頗能相人。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Wen, Guo Jian, and Ma Taichu had privately discussed prognostic texts and omens with Yong Dao's household slave Bi Qingshou. Bi Qingshou told Yong Dao: "Guo Jian is quite skilled at reading faces."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cui Wen, Guo Jian, and Ma Taichu had privately discussed omens and prognostic writings with Yong Dao's slave Bi Qingshou. Bi Qingshou told Yong Dao: "Guo Jian is rather good at physiognomy."

sentences.zh: 永蹈乃召郭諫相已及妻子。

translations.literal: Yong Dao then summoned Guo Jian to read the faces of himself and his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Dao thereupon summoned Guo Jian to read his own face and those of his wife and sons.

sentences.zh: 諫說永蹈曰：「大王相貌非常，王妃及二子皆大貴。」

translations.literal: Jian said to Yong Dao: "Great Prince, your appearance is extraordinary; the princess consort and your two sons are all destined for great eminence."
translations.idiomatic: Jian told Yong Dao: "Your features, Great Prince, are extraordinary; your consort and both sons are marked for the highest fortune."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「大王，元妃長子，不與諸王比也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Great Prince, as the primary consort's eldest son, you are not to be compared with the other princes."
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Great Prince, as the primary consort's eldest son, you stand apart from the other princes altogether."

sentences.zh: 永蹈召崔溫、馬太初論讖記天象。

translations.literal: Yong Dao summoned Cui Wen and Ma Taichu to discuss prognostic texts and celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Dao then called in Cui Wen and Ma Taichu to discuss prognostic writings and the signs in the heavens.

sentences.zh: 崔溫曰：「醜年有兵災，屬兔命者來年春當收兵得位。」

translations.literal: Cui Wen said: "In the year of the Ox there will be military disaster; one born in the year of the Rabbit shall lay down arms and take the throne in the coming spring."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wen said: "In the year of the Ox there will be war; someone born in the year of the Rabbit will sheathe the armies and take the throne the following spring."

sentences.zh: 郭諫曰：「昨見赤氣犯紫微，白虹貫月，皆注醜後寅前兵戈慄亂事。」

translations.literal: Guo Jian said: "Yesterday I saw red vapor assail the Purple Forbidden Enclosure and a white rainbow pierce the moon — both portend armed turmoil and usurpation between the Ox and the Tiger."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jian said: "Yesterday I saw red vapor strike the Purple Forbidden Enclosure and a white rainbow pierce the moon — both foretell war and rebellion between the Ox year and the Tiger."

sentences.zh: 永蹈深信其說，乃陰結內侍鄭雨兒伺上起居，以崔溫為謀主，郭諫、馬太初往來遊說。

translations.literal: Yong Dao deeply believed these explanations. He secretly won over the inner attendant Zheng Yu'er to watch the emperor's movements, made Cui Wen his chief plotter, and had Guo Jian and Ma Taichu go about winning people over.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Dao believed them utterly. He secretly enlisted the eunuch Zheng Yu'er to spy on the emperor's comings and goings, made Cui Wen his chief strategist, and set Guo Jian and Ma Taichu to canvass support.

sentences.zh: 河南統軍使僕散揆尚永蹈妹韓國公主，永蹈謀取河南軍以為助，與妹澤國公主長樂謀，使駙馬都尉蒲剌睹致書於揆，且先請婚，以觀其意。

translations.literal: Pusan Kui, commander of the Henan army, was married to Yong Dao's younger sister, Princess of Han State. Yong Dao plotted to win the Henan army as support; with his younger sister Princess Changle of Ze State he schemed to have the Commandant-escort Pula'adu write to Kui, and first to request a marriage alliance, so as to test his intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Kui, who commanded the Henan army, was married to Yong Dao's sister, the Princess of Han. Yong Dao plotted to bring the Henan forces over to his side. With his sister Changle, Princess of Ze, he had the imperial son-in-law Pula'adu write to Kui and first propose a marriage tie to sound him out.

sentences.zh: 揆拒不許結婚，使者不敢複言不軌事。

translations.literal: Kui refused to permit the marriage, and the envoy dared not again speak of treasonous matters.
translations.idiomatic: Kui refused the match, and the messenger did not dare broach sedition again.

sentences.zh: 永蹈家奴董壽諫永蹈，不聽。

translations.literal: Yong Dao's household slave Dong Shou remonstrated with Yong Dao, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Dao's slave Dong Shou tried to dissuade him, but he would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 董壽以語同輩奴千家奴，上變。

translations.literal: Dong Shou told this to his fellow slave Qianjianu, who reported the plot to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shou told a fellow slave named Qianjianu, who laid the matter before the throne.

sentences.zh: 是時，永蹈在京師，詔平章政事完顏守貞、參知政事胥持國、戶部尚書楊伯通、知大興府事尼龐古鑒鞫問，連引甚眾，久不能決。

translations.literal: At this time Yong Dao was in the capital. An edict ordered Grand Councilor Wanyan Shouzhen, Vice Director Xu Chiguo, Minister of Revenue Yang Botong, and Administrator of Daxing Prefecture Nipanggu Jian to interrogate the case; many were implicated by association, and for a long time no decision could be reached.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Dao was then in the capital. The court ordered Grand Councilor Wanyan Shouzhen, Vice Director Xu Chiguo, Revenue Minister Yang Botong, and Daxing prefect Nipanggu Jian to investigate. The net of implication grew very wide, and for a long time no verdict could be reached.

sentences.zh: 上怒，召守貞等問狀。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and summoned Shouzhen and the others to report on the case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and summoned Shouzhen and the rest to account for the delay.

sentences.zh: 右丞相夾谷清臣奏曰：「事貴速絕，以安人心。」

translations.literal: Right Director Jiagu Qingchen memorialized: "Matters should be settled swiftly to reassure the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Right Director Jiagu Qingchen submitted: "This affair must be ended quickly if hearts are to be steadied."

sentences.zh: 於是，賜永蹈及妃卞玉，二子按春、阿辛，公主長樂自盡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yong Dao and his consort Bian Yu, his two sons Anchun and Axin, and Princess Changle were granted death by suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yong Dao, his consort Bian Yu, his sons Anchun and Axin, and Princess Changle were all allowed to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 蒲剌睹、崔溫、郭諫、馬太初等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Pula'adu, Cui Wen, Guo Jian, Ma Taichu, and the rest were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Pula'adu, Cui Wen, Guo Jian, Ma Taichu, and the others were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 僕散揆雖不聞問，猶坐除名。

translations.literal: Though Pusan Kui was not charged in the inquiry, he was still stripped of his name and office.
translations.idiomatic: Though Pusan Kui was never formally tried, he was still removed from office and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 董壽免死，隸監籍。

translations.literal: Dong Shou was spared death and enrolled in supervised service.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shou was spared execution and placed on the supervised register.

sentences.zh: 千家奴賞錢二千貫，特遷五官雜班敘使。

translations.literal: Qianjianu was rewarded with two thousand strings of cash and specially promoted to clerk of the Five Offices mixed roster.
translations.idiomatic: Qianjianu was rewarded with two thousand strings of cash and specially promoted to clerk in the Five Offices mixed roster.

sentences.zh: 自是諸王制限防禁密矣。

translations.literal: From this point the restrictions and surveillance placed on princes grew strict indeed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the curbs and surveillance imposed on the princes grew far tighter.

sentences.zh: 泰和七年，詔複王封，備禮改葬，賜諡曰剌，以衛王永濟子按辰為永蹈後，奉其祭祀。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe, an edict restored his princely title; he was reburied with full rites and granted the posthumous name La. An Chen, son of Prince of Wei Yong Ji, was made Yong Dao's heir to perform the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taihe an edict restored his princely rank; he was reburied with full honors and given the posthumous name La. An Chen, son of Prince Wei Yong Ji, was appointed Yong Dao's heir to maintain his ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 越王永功，本名宋葛，又名廣孫，貞元二年生。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Yong Gong, original name Songge, also called Guangsun, was born in the second year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gong, Prince of Yue, born Songge and also known as Guangsun, was born in the second year of Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 沉默寡言笑，勇健絕人，涉書史，好法書名畫。

translations.literal: Silent and sparing of speech and laughter, surpassingly brave and strong, versed in books and history, fond of model calligraphy and famous paintings.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and sparing of words and laughter, he was unmatched in courage and strength, well read in history, and devoted to fine calligraphy and celebrated paintings.

sentences.zh: 大定四年，封鄭王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dading, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dading he was made Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 七年，進封隋王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was advanced to Prince of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Prince of Sui.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進封曹王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was advanced to Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 十五年，除刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「侍郎張汝霖，汝外舅行也，可學為政。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Vice Director Zhang Rulin is of your maternal uncle's generation; you may learn governance from him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Vice Director Zhang Rulin stands in your maternal uncle's generation — you may learn the art of governing from him."

sentences.zh: 十七年，授活活土世襲猛安。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was granted the hereditary meng'an of Huohuotu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was granted the hereditary meng'an of Huohuotu.

sentences.zh: 十八年，改大興尹。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was transferred to be Administrator of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was made Administrator of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 世宗幸金蓮川，始出中都，親軍二蒼頭縱馬食民田，詔永功：「蒼頭各杖一百。

translations.literal: When Shizong visited Jinlianchuan and first left the Central Capital, two personal attendants of the imperial guard let their horses graze on the people's fields. An edict to Yong Gong read: "Each attendant is to be beaten one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong went to Jinlianchuan and left the Central Capital for the first time, two attendants of the imperial guard let their horses graze in the people's fields. The court ordered Yong Gong: "Beat each attendant a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 彈壓百戶二人失覺察，勒停。」

translations.literal: The two company commanders charged with keeping order had failed to notice; they were ordered to cease service."
translations.idiomatic: The two centurions responsible for keeping order had failed to notice; they were ordered to stand down from duty."

sentences.zh: 上次望京澱，永功奏曰：「親軍人止一蒼頭、兩彈壓服勤，為日久矣。

translations.literal: When Shizong last visited Jingdian, Yong Gong memorialized: "The imperial guard had only one attendant and two centurions on duty — they had served long.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizong's last visit to Jingdian, Yong Gong reported: "The imperial guard had only one attendant and two centurions standing watch — they had been at it a long time.

sentences.zh: 臣昧死違詔，量決蒼頭，使彈壓待罪，可使償其田直，惟陛下憐察。」

translations.literal: I dare disobey the edict and have judged the attendant according to circumstances, leaving the centurions to await punishment; they can compensate the value of the fields — I beg Your Majesty's compassionate understanding."
translations.idiomatic: I have ventured to go beyond the edict in punishing the attendant as circumstances warranted, while leaving the centurions to await sentence; they can make good the damage to the fields — I beg Your Majesty to look on this with compassion."

sentences.zh: 上皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved it all.

sentences.zh: 老嫗與男婦憩道傍，婦與所私相從亡去，或告嫗曰：「向見年少婦人自水邊小徑去矣。」

translations.literal: An old woman and her son's wife rested by the roadside; the wife ran off with her lover. Someone told the old woman: "I just saw a young woman go off along the small path by the water."
translations.idiomatic: An old woman and her daughter-in-law rested by the road; the wife slipped away with her lover. Someone told the old woman: "I saw a young woman take the footpath along the water just now."

sentences.zh: 嫗告伍長蹤跡之。

translations.literal: The old woman told the squad chief to track her.
translations.idiomatic: The old woman reported this to the squad chief and asked him to follow her trail.

sentences.zh: 有男子私殺牛，手持血刃，望見伍長，意其捕己，即走避之。

translations.literal: A man who had secretly slaughtered an ox, bloody knife in hand, saw the squad chief, thought he had come to seize him, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A man who had butchered an ox in secret, still holding a bloody knife, caught sight of the squad chief, assumed he was about to be arrested, and ran.

sentences.zh: 嫗與伍長疑是殺其婦也，捕送縣，不勝楚毒，遂誣服。

translations.literal: The old woman and the squad chief suspected he had killed her daughter-in-law; he was seized and sent to the county, could not endure the torture, and falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The old woman and the squad chief took him for the murderer of the daughter-in-law; he was hauled to the county seat, broke under torture, and confessed to a crime he had not committed.

sentences.zh: 問屍安在？

translations.literal: They asked where the corpse was.
translations.idiomatic: They asked where the body was.

sentences.zh: 詭曰：「棄之水中矣。」

translations.literal: He lied, saying: "I threw it into the water."
translations.idiomatic: He lied: "I threw it in the river."

sentences.zh: 求之水中，果獲一屍，已半腐。

translations.literal: They searched the water and indeed recovered a corpse, already half decayed.
translations.idiomatic: They dragged the river and found a corpse, already half decomposed.

sentences.zh: 縣吏以為是男子真殺若婦矣，即具獄上。

translations.literal: The county clerks thought this man had truly killed the woman and at once prepared the case for submission.
translations.idiomatic: The county officials concluded the man had indeed killed her and drew up the case for the higher authorities.

sentences.zh: 永功疑之曰：「婦死幾何日，而屍遽半腐哉。」

translations.literal: Yong Gong was doubtful and said: "How many days since the woman died, that the corpse should already be half decayed?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gong had his doubts: "How long could she have been dead for the body to be half rotted already?"

sentences.zh: 頃之，嫗得其婦於所私者。

translations.literal: Before long the old woman recovered her daughter-in-law from the lover.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the old woman found her daughter-in-law with the lover.

sentences.zh: 永功曰：「是男子偶以殺人就獄，其拷掠足以稱殺牛之科矣。」

translations.literal: Yong Gong said: "This man happened to enter prison on a murder charge; the beating he suffered is punishment enough for slaughtering an ox."
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gong said: "The man was thrown into jail on a murder charge by chance; what he has already endured in interrogation is punishment enough for killing an ox."

sentences.zh: 遂釋之而去。

translations.literal: He was then released and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: He was released and sent on his way.

sentences.zh: 武清黃氏、望雲王氏豪猾不逞，永功發其罪，畿內肅然。

translations.literal: The Huang clan of Wuqing and the Wang clan of Wangyun were overbearing and lawless; Yong Gong exposed their crimes, and the capital region grew orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The Huang of Wuqing and the Wang of Wangyun were powerful bullies; Yong Gong exposed their crimes, and the capital district grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，判東京留守。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was appointed to serve as Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was made regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 是月，改河間尹。

translations.literal: That same month he was transferred to be Administrator of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: That month he was reassigned as Administrator of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 閱月，改北京留守。

translations.literal: After a month he was transferred to be Northern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was made regent of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 居無何，上謂宰臣曰：「朕聞永功到北京為政無良，雖朕子，萬一敗露，法可廢乎。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor told the chief ministers: "I hear that Yong Gong's governance at the Northern Capital has been poor. Though he is my son, if misconduct should come to light, can the law be set aside?
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor told his ministers: "I hear Yong Gong has governed badly at the Northern Capital. He is my son, but if wrongdoing comes to light, can the law be waived?

sentences.zh: 朕已戒敕永功，卿等可諭其長史，俾匡正之。」

translations.literal: I have already admonished Yong Gong; you may instruct his chief administrator to correct him."
translations.idiomatic: I have already warned Yong Gong; you should tell his chief administrator to set him straight."

sentences.zh: 到北京凡七月，改東京留守。

translations.literal: After seven months at the Northern Capital he was transferred to be Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: After seven months in the north he was reassigned as regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗幸上京，過東京，永功從。

translations.literal: When Shizong visited the Upper Capital and passed through the Eastern Capital, Yong Gong accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong went to the Upper Capital and passed through the Eastern Capital, Yong Gong went with him.

sentences.zh: 明年，上還至天平山好水川，皇太子薨。

translations.literal: The next year, as the emperor returned to Haoshuichuan at Tianping Mountain, the crown prince died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, as the emperor was returning to Haoshuichuan on Tianping Mountain, the crown prince died.

sentences.zh: 詔永功護喪事，尋拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yong Gong to oversee the funeral; he was soon appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gong was ordered to supervise the funeral rites and was soon made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 章宗封原王，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Zhangzong was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuan and granted the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong was made Prince of Yuan and given the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 趙王永中及永功兄弟皆加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Yong Zhong and Yong Gong's brothers were all granted the same rank.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Yong Zhong and Yong Gong's brothers received the same honor.

sentences.zh: 明年，判大宗正事。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed to direct the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was put in charge of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 應州僧與永功有舊，將訴事于彰國軍節度使移剌胡剌，求永功手書與胡剌為地。

translations.literal: A monk of Yingzhou who was old acquaintance of Yong Gong was about to plead a case before Yelü Hula, military commissioner of Zhangguo Army, and asked Yong Gong for a letter in his own hand to Hula to pave the way.
translations.idiomatic: A monk from Yingzhou who knew Yong Gong was going to bring a grievance before Yelü Hula, commissioner of the Zhangguo army, and asked Yong Gong for a personal letter to smooth the way with Hula.

sentences.zh: 胡剌得書，奏之。

translations.literal: Hula received the letter and memorialized about it.
translations.idiomatic: Hula received the letter and reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰臣曰：「永功以書囑事胡剌，此雖細微，不可不懲也。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers: "Yong Gong used a letter to entrust a matter to Hula. Though this is a small thing, it cannot go unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers: "Yong Gong used a letter to ask Hula to handle a matter for him. Small as it is, it cannot go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 凡人小過不治，遂至大咎。

translations.literal: If a man's small faults are not corrected, they lead to great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When small faults go uncorrected, they grow into great disasters.

sentences.zh: 有犯必懲，庶幾能改，是亦教也。」

translations.literal: When there is an offense, punishment must follow; then one may hope for reform — this too is instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Punish every offense, and there is hope of reform — that itself is a form of teaching."

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「陛下用法無私，臣下敢不敬畏。」

translations.literal: All said: "Your Majesty applies the law without partiality; how dare your servants not stand in awe?"
translations.idiomatic: All said: "Your Majesty applies the law without favor; how could we servants not revere it?"

sentences.zh: 於是永功解職。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yong Gong was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gong was then dismissed from his post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，複判大宗正事。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed to direct the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to head the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，除判平陽府事，進封冀王。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, Yong Gong was appointed to administer Pingyang Prefecture and advanced to Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong came to the throne, Yong Gong was put in charge of Pingyang Prefecture and promoted to Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 永功之官，隨引醫人沈思存過制限，當解職。

translations.literal: In Yong Gong's office he had brought in the physician Shen Sicun beyond the prescribed limit and ought to have been removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: At Yong Gong's post he had brought in the physician Shen Sicun beyond the prescribed limit and should have been dismissed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕知此事，當痛斷監奴及治府掾長史管轄府事者罪，仍著於令。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I know of this matter. The supervising slaves and the chief administrator who governed the prefectural office must be punished severely, and this shall be written into the regulations."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I know of this. The supervising slaves and the chief administrator who governed the prefectural office must be punished severely, and this shall be written into the regulations."

sentences.zh: 家奴王唐犯罪至徒，永功曲庇之。

translations.literal: The household slave Wang Tang had committed an offense punishable by penal servitude, and Yong Gong shielded him improperly.
translations.idiomatic: His household slave Wang Tang had committed an offense punishable by penal servitude, and Yong Gong improperly shielded him.

sentences.zh: 平陽治中高德裔失覺察，笞四十。

translations.literal: Gao Deyi, assistant administrator of Pingyang, failed to detect it and was beaten forty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Deyi, assistant administrator of Pingyang, failed to notice it and was flogged forty strokes.

sentences.zh: 於是永功改判濟南府。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yong Gong was transferred to administer Jinan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Gong was then reassigned to administer Jinan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔永功曰：「所坐雖細事，法令不得不如此。

translations.literal: An edict to Yong Gong read: "Though the offense is a small matter, the law cannot be applied otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: An edict told Yong Gong: "Though the offense is a small matter, the law cannot be applied otherwise.

sentences.zh: 今已釋矣，後毋複然。

translations.literal: You are now released. Do not let it happen again.
translations.idiomatic: You are released now. Do not let it happen again.

sentences.zh: 濟南先帝舊治，風土甚好，可悉此意也。」

translations.literal: Jinan was the late emperor's former seat of rule, and its customs and land are very fine. Keep this fully in mind."
translations.idiomatic: Jinan was the late emperor's former seat of government, and its customs and land are excellent. Keep this fully in mind."

sentences.zh: 改授山東西路把魯古世襲猛安。

translations.literal: He was transferred and granted the hereditary meng'an of Balugu on the Shandong Western Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned and granted the hereditary meng'an of Balugu in western Shandong.

sentences.zh: 二年，判廣寧府事，進封魯王。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed to administer Guangning Prefecture and advanced to Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was put in charge of Guangning Prefecture and promoted to Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 明年，判彰德府事。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed to administer Zhangde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was put in charge of Zhangde Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 承安元年，進封郢王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Cheng'an he was advanced to Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Cheng'an he was promoted to Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 明年，判太原府事。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed to administer Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was put in charge of Taiyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泰和七年，改西京留守。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe he was transferred to Western Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taihe he was made regent of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 八年，複判平陽府事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was again appointed to administer Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was again put in charge of Pingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大安元年，進封譙王，判中山府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Da'an he was advanced to Prince of Qiao and appointed to administer Zhongshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Da'an he was promoted to Prince of Qiao and put in charge of Zhongshan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，進封越王。

translations.literal: The next year he was advanced to Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，免常參。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, Yong Gong was excused from regular court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong came to the throne, Yong Gong was excused from daily court attendance.

sentences.zh: 明年，從遷汴京。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the court in moving to Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he followed the court's move to Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 久之，詔永功每月朔一朝。

translations.literal: After a long while, an edict ordered Yong Gong to attend court once on the first of each month.
translations.idiomatic: After some time an edict required Yong Gong to attend court on the first day of each month.

sentences.zh: 興定四年，詔永功無朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xingding, an edict excused Yong Gong from court attendance altogether.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xingding an edict relieved Yong Gong of all court attendance.

sentences.zh: 五年，有疾，賜禦藥。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he fell ill and was granted imperial medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he fell ill and was given medicine from the imperial pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 疾革，賜尚醫診視，一日五遣使候問。

translations.literal: When his illness grew critical, court physicians were sent to examine him; five times a day messengers were dispatched to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned grave, imperial physicians were sent to treat him, and five times a day couriers were sent to ask after him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died.

sentences.zh: 上哭之慟，諡曰忠簡。

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him bitterly and granted the posthumous name Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply and gave him the posthumous name Zhongjian.

sentences.zh: 子福孫、壽孫、粘沒曷。

translations.literal: His sons were Fusun, Shousun, and Zhanmoye.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Fusun, Shousun, and Zhanmoye.

sentences.zh: 大定二十六年，詔賜福孫名璐，壽孫名璹，粘沒曷名琳。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Dading, an edict granted Fusun the name Lu, Shousun the name Shu, and Zhanmoye the name Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Dading an edict gave Fusun the name Lu, Shousun the name Shu, and Zhanmoye the name Lin.

sentences.zh: 是年，璐加奉國上將軍。

translations.literal: That year Lu was promoted to General-in-Chief Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lu was made General-in-Chief Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，加銀青榮祿大夫，封蕭國公。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, Lu was made Silver-Green Glory Grandee and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao State.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong came to the throne, Lu was made Silver-Green Glory Grandee and created Duke of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 初為興陵崇妃養子，常居京師，奉朝請。

translations.literal: He had early been adopted son of the Chong consort of Xingling and constantly resided in the capital, attending court as required.
translations.idiomatic: He had been adopted in youth by the Chong consort of Xingling, lived permanently in the capital, and attended court on summons.

sentences.zh: 泰和五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 章宗輟朝，百官進名奉慰。

translations.literal: Zhangzong suspended court; the officials presented their names to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong suspended court, and the officials presented their names in condolence.

sentences.zh: 子 璹

translations.literal: Son: Shu
translations.idiomatic: His son: Shu

sentences.zh: 璹本名壽孫，世宗賜名，字仲實，一字子瑜。

translations.literal: Shu, original name Shousun, was given his name by Shizong. His style was Zhongshi, and he also used the style Ziyu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, born Shousun, received his name from Shizong. His style was Zhongshi, and he also went by Ziyu.

sentences.zh: 資質簡重，博學有俊才，喜為詩，工真草書。

translations.literal: Of plain and weighty character, broadly learned and possessed of outstanding talent, he delighted in composing poetry and was skilled in regular and cursive script.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and grave in manner, widely learned and brilliantly gifted, he loved poetry and excelled in both regular and cursive calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 大定二十七年，加奉國上將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Dading he was promoted to General-in-Chief Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Dading he was made General-in-Chief Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 明昌初，加銀青榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingchang he was made Silver-Green Glory Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Mingchang he was made Silver-Green Glory Grandee.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王時，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: During the reign of Prince of Wei-Shao he was granted Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Prince Wei-Shao he was given the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 貞佑中，封胙國公。

translations.literal: During Zhenyou he was enfeoffed as Duke of Zuo State.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyou he was made Duke of Zuo.

sentences.zh: 正大初，進封密國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengda he was advanced to Duke of Mi State.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengda he was promoted to Duke of Mi.

sentences.zh: 璹奉朝請四十年，日以講誦吟詠為事，時時潛與士大夫唱酬，然不敢明白往來。

translations.literal: Shu attended court on summons for forty years, spending his days in study, recitation, and verse; from time to time he secretly exchanged poems with scholar-officials, yet did not dare to associate openly.
translations.idiomatic: For forty years Shu lived on court summons, devoting his days to study, recitation, and poetry; he would quietly exchange verses with scholar-officials, but never dared to visit them openly.

sentences.zh: 永功薨後，稍得出遊，與文士趙秉文、楊雲翼、雷淵、元好問、李汾、王飛伯輩交善。

translations.literal: After Yong Gong's death he was able to travel somewhat more freely and formed friendships with the literary men Zhao Bingwen, Yang Yunyi, Lei Yuan, Yuan Haowen, Li Fen, Wang Feibo, and their kind.
translations.idiomatic: After Yong Gong died he was able to travel more freely and became close to the literati Zhao Bingwen, Yang Yunyi, Lei Yuan, Yuan Haowen, Li Fen, Wang Feibo, and others of that circle.

sentences.zh: 初，宣宗南遷，諸王宗室顛沛奔走，璹乃盡載其家法書名畫，一帙不遺。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong moved south, the princes and imperial clan fled in disorder; Shu loaded all his family's model calligraphy and famous paintings, not leaving a single scroll behind.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong moved the court south, the princes and imperial kin scattered in turmoil; Shu took along every scroll of his family's calligraphy and paintings without losing a single one.

sentences.zh: 居汴中，家人口多，俸入少，客至，貧不能具酒肴，蔬飯共食，焚香煮茗，盡出藏書，談大定、明昌以來故事，終日不聽客去，樂而不厭也。

translations.literal: Living in Bian, his household was large and his salary small. When guests came he was too poor to set out wine and meat; they shared plain vegetable meals, burned incense and brewed tea, brought out all his stored books, and talked of events since Dading and Mingchang — all day he would not let guests leave, delighting in it without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: In Bian his household was large and his income thin. When guests arrived he could not afford a proper feast; they ate simple vegetable meals together, burned incense and brewed tea, brought out his whole library, and talked of times since Dading and Mingchang — he would keep them all day and never tire of it.

sentences.zh: 天興初，璹已臥疾，論及時事，歎曰：「兵勢如此，不能支，止可以降。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing Shu was already bedridden with illness. Discussing current affairs, he sighed and said: "With the military situation like this, it cannot be sustained; we can only surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianxing Shu was already bedridden. Discussing current affairs, he sighed and said: "With the military situation like this, we cannot hold out; we can only surrender.

sentences.zh: 全完顏氏一族歸吾國中，使女直不滅則善矣，余複何望。」

translations.literal: If the whole Wanyan clan can be preserved within our state so that the Jurchens are not extinguished, that would be well enough; what more could I hope for?"
translations.idiomatic: If the whole Wanyan clan can be preserved within our state so that the Jurchens are not wiped out, that would be enough; what more could I hope for?"

sentences.zh: 是時，曹王出質，璹見哀宗於隆德殿。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Cao was sent out as hostage; Shu had an audience with Emperor Aizong in Longde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Cao was sent out as a hostage; Shu had an audience with Emperor Aizong in Longde Hall.

sentences.zh: 上問：「叔父欲何言？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "What does Uncle wish to say?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "What does Uncle wish to say?"

sentences.zh: 璹奏曰：「聞訛可欲出議和。

translations.literal: Shu memorialized: "I hear that Eke wishes to go out to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shu reported: "I hear that Eke wishes to go out to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 訛可年幼，不苦諳練，恐不能辦大事。

translations.literal: Eke is young and not well practiced; I fear he cannot manage so great a matter.
translations.idiomatic: Eke is young and not well practiced; I fear he cannot manage so great a matter.

sentences.zh: 臣請副之，或代其行。」

translations.literal: Your servant asks to accompany him, or to go in his place."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to accompany him, or to go in his place."

sentences.zh: 上慰之曰：「南渡後，國家比承平時有何奉養，然叔父亦未嘗沾溉。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him, saying: "After the move south, what support has the state had compared with times of peace? Yet Uncle too has never shared in its bounty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him, saying: "After the move south, what support has the state had compared with times of peace? Yet Uncle too has never shared in its bounty.

sentences.zh: 無事則置之冷地，無所顧藉，緩急則置於不測，叔父盡忠固可，天下其謂朕何？

translations.literal: When there is no trouble you are left in the cold with nothing to rely on; in crisis you are placed in peril. Uncle's loyalty is certainly real, but what will the realm say of me?
translations.idiomatic: When there is no trouble you are left in the cold with nothing to rely on; in crisis you are placed in peril. Uncle's loyalty is certainly real, but what will the realm say of me?

sentences.zh: 叔父休矣。」

translations.literal: Uncle, say no more."
translations.idiomatic: Uncle, say no more."

sentences.zh: 於是君臣相顧泣下。

translations.literal: Thereupon sovereign and minister looked at one another and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereign and minister then looked at one another and wept.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾薨。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 年六十一。

translations.literal: He was sixty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 平生詩文甚多。

translations.literal: In his lifetime he wrote a great deal of poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: Over his lifetime he wrote a great deal of poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 自刪其詩，存三百首，樂府一百首，號《如庵小稿》。

translations.literal: He himself culled his poems, keeping three hundred and one hundred yuefu pieces, under the title Minor Drafts from the Ru'an Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He edited his own poems down to three hundred pieces and a hundred yuefu lyrics, collected under the title Minor Drafts from the Ru'an Studio.

sentences.zh: 第五子守禧，字慶之，風神秀徹，璹特鍾愛，嘗曰：「平日所蓄書畫將以付斯子。」

translations.literal: His fifth son Shouxi, style Qingzhi, was graceful and clear in bearing; Shu cherished him above all and once said: "The books and paintings I have gathered over the years shall be given to this son."
translations.idiomatic: His fifth son Shouxi, styled Qingzhi, was exceptionally refined in bearing; Shu doted on him and once said: "The books and paintings I have collected through the years will go to this boy."

sentences.zh: 及汴城降，守禧病卒，年未三十。

translations.literal: When Bian fell, Shouxi died of illness, not yet thirty years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian fell, Shouxi died of illness before he was thirty.

sentences.zh: 潞王永德，本名訛出。

translations.literal: Prince of Lu Yong De, original name Echu.
translations.idiomatic: Yong De, Prince of Lu, born Echu.

sentences.zh: 大定二十五年，與章宗及諸兄俱加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Dading he, Zhangzong, and all the elder princes were granted the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Dading he, Zhangzong, and all the elder princes were given the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，封薛王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was made Prince of Xue.

sentences.zh: 明年，除秘書監。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed to direct the Directorate of Archives.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was put in charge of the Directorate of Archives.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，進判秘書監，進封沈王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was advanced to supervising director of the Directorate of Archives and promoted to Prince of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was made supervising director of the Directorate of Archives and promoted to Prince of Shen.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，授山東東路把魯古必剌猛安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingchang he was granted the Balugu Bila meng'an on the Shandong Eastern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Mingchang he received the Balugu Bila meng'an in eastern Shandong.

sentences.zh: 二年，進封豳王。

translations.literal: In the second year he was advanced to Prince of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to Prince of Bin.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷勸農使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，進封潞王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an he was advanced to Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Cheng'an he was promoted to Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 承安三年，再任勸農使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Cheng'an he again served as Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Cheng'an he again served as Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，有司劾永德元日進酒後期，有詔勿問。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe the authorities impeached Yong De for presenting New Year's wine late; an edict ordered that the matter not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taihe the authorities impeached Yong De for presenting New Year's wine late; an edict ordered that the matter be dropped.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王時，累遷太子太師。

translations.literal: During the reign of Prince of Wei-Shao he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Prince Wei-Shao he rose repeatedly to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，改同判大睦親府事。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, he was transferred to associate director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong came to the throne, he was made associate director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 興定五年，遷判大睦親府事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xingding he was transferred to director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xingding he was made director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 子斡論，賜名琰。

translations.literal: His son Wolun was granted the name Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wolun was given the name Yan.

sentences.zh: 豫王永成，本名鶴野，又曰婁室。

translations.literal: Prince of Yu Yong Cheng, original name Heye, also called Loushi.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Cheng, Prince of Yu, born Heye and also known as Loushi.

sentences.zh: 母昭儀梁氏。

translations.literal: His mother was the zhaoyi Lady Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Liang, a zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 永成風姿奇偉，博學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Yong Cheng's bearing was singular and imposing; he was broadly learned and skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Cheng was striking in appearance, widely learned, and a gifted writer.

sentences.zh: 世宗尤愛重之。

translations.literal: Shizong cherished him above all others.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong loved and valued him above all his sons.

sentences.zh: 大定七年，始封沈王，以太學博士王彥潛為府文學，永成師事之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dading he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Shen; Wang Yanqian, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, was made literary instructor of the princely household, and Yong Cheng studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dading he was first made Prince of Shen; Wang Yanqian of the Imperial Academy was appointed literary tutor to his household, and Yong Cheng studied under him.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進封豳。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was advanced to Prince of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Prince of Bin.

sentences.zh: 十五年，就外第。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he took up residence outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he moved to an estate outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 十六年，判秘書監。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed to direct the Directorate of Archives.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was put in charge of the Directorate of Archives.

sentences.zh: 明年，授世襲山東東路把魯古猛安，判大睦親府事。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted the hereditary meng'an of Balugu on the Shandong Eastern Circuit and appointed to direct the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received the hereditary meng'an of Balugu in eastern Shandong and was made director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 既而改中都路胡土靄哥蠻猛安。

translations.literal: Soon after he was transferred to the meng'an of Hutu'aige on the Central Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned to the meng'an of Hutu'aige on the Central Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十年，改授翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was transferred to be Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was made chief academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，判定武軍節度使事，尋改判廣寧府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed military commissioner of Dingwu Army; soon after he was transferred to administer Guangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was made commissioner of the Dingwu army; soon after he was reassigned to administer Guangning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，世宗幸上京，命留守中都，判吏部尚書，進開府儀同三司，為御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, when Shizong visited the Upper Capital, Yong Cheng was ordered to remain and guard the Central Capital, to serve as Minister of Personnel, was advanced to Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, when Shizong went to the Upper Capital, Yong Cheng was left to guard the Central Capital, given charge of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，起複，進封吳，判真定府事。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, Yong Cheng was recalled to service, advanced to Prince of Wu, and appointed to administer Zhending Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong came to the throne, Yong Cheng was recalled, made Prince of Wu, and put in charge of Zhending Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，改山東西路盆買必剌猛安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingchang he was transferred to the meng'an of Penmaibila on the Shandong Western Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Mingchang he was reassigned to the meng'an of Penmaibila in western Shandong.

sentences.zh: 明年，進封兗。

translations.literal: The next year he was advanced to Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 坐率軍民圍獵，解職，奉表謝罪。

translations.literal: Because he had led soldiers and civilians in a battue hunt, he was removed from office and submitted a memorial asking forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for leading troops and civilians on a battue hunt and submitted a memorial of apology.

sentences.zh: 上賜手詔曰：「卿親實肺腑，夙著忠純，侍顯考于春宮，曲盡友于之愛，洎沖人之繼統，愈明忠赤之心，艱難之中，多所裨益。

translations.literal: The emperor granted a personal edict saying: "You are kin in truth, flesh of my flesh, long known for loyalty and purity. You served my late father in the Eastern Palace and fulfilled brotherly love to the utmost; when the young ruler succeeded, your loyal heart grew still clearer, and in hard times you rendered much aid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a personal edict: "You are truly of my own flesh, long famed for loyalty. You served my late father in the Eastern Palace with perfect brotherly devotion; when the young sovereign succeeded, your loyal heart shone all the brighter, and in hardship you gave much help.

sentences.zh: 朕心簡在，毫楮莫窮，用是起之苫塊之中，授以維城之任。

translations.literal: My heart holds you close — no brush could exhaust it — and therefore I raised you from deepest mourning and entrusted you with the charge of guarding the realm.
translations.idiomatic: My heart holds you close beyond what words can tell; that is why I raised you from mourning and gave you the charge of guarding the realm.

sentences.zh: 自典籓服，歲月薦更，蕞爾趙邦，知驥足之難展，眇哉鎮府，固牛刀之莫施。

translations.literal: Since you have governed a fief, years have passed in turn; in tiny Zhao you found a steed's legs hard to stretch, and in a petty commandery a butcher's knife could scarcely be wielded.
translations.idiomatic: Since you took up a fief the years have turned; in petty Zhao you found no room for a thoroughbred's stride, and in so small a prefecture even a master butcher's knife had little to cut.

sentences.zh: 方思驛召以赴朝，何意遽罹于國憲。

translations.literal: I was just thinking to summon you post-haste to court — how could I expect you suddenly to fall under the state's law?
translations.idiomatic: I was about to summon you urgently to court — who would have thought you would suddenly run afoul of the law?

sentences.zh: 偶因時獵，頗擾部民，法所不寬，憲台聞上。

translations.literal: By chance you hunted at the season and greatly disturbed the people under your command; the law cannot overlook this, and the Censorate reported it to me.
