translations.idiomatic: You happened to hunt at the season and greatly disturbed the people under your command; the law cannot excuse it, and the Censorate reported it to me.

sentences.zh: 朕尚含容累月，未忍即行，雖欲遂於私恩，竟莫違于公議，解卿前職，即乃世封。

translations.literal: I bore with it for months and could not bear to act at once; though I wished to follow private affection, in the end I could not go against public opinion — I relieve you of your former post but leave your hereditary enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: I bore with it for months and could not bring myself to act; though I wished to honor private feeling, I could not defy public opinion — I remove you from your former post but leave your hereditary title intact.

sentences.zh: 噫，祖宗立法，非一人之敢私；

translations.literal: Alas — the laws our ancestors established are not for any one man to set aside privately;
translations.idiomatic: Alas — the laws our ancestors laid down are not for any one man to bend to private ends;

sentences.zh: 骨肉至親，豈千里而能間。

translations.literal: flesh-and-blood kin closest of all — can a thousand li come between us?
translations.idiomatic: kin of flesh and blood — can a thousand li put us apart?

sentences.zh: 以此退閑之小誡，欲成終始之洪恩。

translations.literal: Take this small rebuke of retirement as leisure, that it may complete a great favor from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: Take this small lesson in withdrawal as the price of a lasting grace between us from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 《經》雲：'在上不驕，高而不危。

translations.literal: The Classic says: 'When one in high place is not arrogant, though lofty he is not in peril.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says: 'He who in high place is not arrogant remains lofty yet unendangered.'

sentences.zh: '是以知節慎者修身之本，驕矜者敗德之源。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that restraint and caution are the root of self-cultivation, and arrogance the source of ruined virtue.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that restraint is the foundation of character, and arrogance the wellspring of moral ruin.

sentences.zh: 朕每自勵，今以戒卿。

translations.literal: I constantly urge myself on this; now I offer it as a warning to you.
translations.idiomatic: I urge myself on this constantly; now I offer it as a warning to you.

sentences.zh: 昔東平樂善，能成不朽之名，梁孝奢淫，卒致憂疑之悔。

translations.literal: Of old, the Prince of Dongping delighted in goodness and won an undying name; Prince Xiao of Liang was extravagant and dissolute and in the end met regret amid suspicion and grief.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Prince of Dongping loved goodness and won an immortal name; Prince Xiao of Liang lived in luxury and lust and ended in sorrow and suspicion.

sentences.zh: 前人所行，可為龜鑑。

translations.literal: What men of former times did may serve as a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The deeds of those who came before may serve as a mirror.

sentences.zh: 卿兼資文武，多藝多才，履道而行，何施不可。

translations.literal: You combine civil and military gifts, many arts and many talents; walk the Way and what could you not accomplish?
translations.idiomatic: You unite civil and military gifts, with many arts and many talents; walk the right path and what could you not achieve?

sentences.zh: 如能德業日新，無慮牽複之晚。

translations.literal: If your virtue and achievement renew themselves day by day, you need not fear that recall will come late.
translations.idiomatic: If your virtue and achievement grow day by day, you need not worry that recall will be long delayed.

sentences.zh: 朕素不工詞翰，臨文草草，直寫所懷，冀不以辭害意也。」

translations.literal: I have never been skilled at letters; when I take up the brush I write hastily, setting down my thoughts directly, hoping the words will not obscure the meaning."
translations.idiomatic: I have never been skilled with the pen; when I write I do so hastily, putting down what I feel directly, in hope that the words will not obscure my meaning."

sentences.zh: 未幾，授沁南軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed military commissioner of Qinnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made commissioner of the Qinnan army.

sentences.zh: 三年，改判咸平府事，未赴，移判太原府事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to administer Xianping Prefecture; before he took up the post he was moved to administer Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was reassigned to Xianping Prefecture; before he could take up the post he was moved to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 上以永成誕日，親為詩以賜，有「美譽自應輝玉牒，忠誠不待啟金滕」之語，當世榮之。

translations.literal: On Yong Cheng's birthday the emperor personally composed a poem to bestow on him, with the lines "Fine repute should naturally shine in the imperial registers; loyalty needs no opening of the golden casket" — men of the age counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: On Yong Cheng's birthday the emperor wrote him a poem in his own hand, including the lines "Fine repute should naturally grace the imperial registers; loyalty needs no golden casket to prove it" — contemporaries regarded it as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 七年，改判平陽府事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to administer Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was reassigned to administer Pingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 承安改元，以覃恩進封豫。

translations.literal: When the Cheng'an era was proclaimed, he was advanced to Prince of Yu as part of a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: At the proclamation of the Cheng'an era he was promoted to Prince of Yu in a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，進馬八十疋，以資守禦之備。

translations.literal: The next winter he presented eighty horses to supply preparations for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he presented eighty horses to help with frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 上賜詔獎諭曰：「卿夙有雋望，時惟茂親，通達古今，砥礪忠義。

translations.literal: The emperor granted an edict of commendation, saying: "You have long enjoyed outstanding repute; you are a flourishing kinsman of the time, versed in past and present, and you temper loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an edict of praise: "You have long enjoyed a fine reputation; you are a flourishing kinsman of our house, versed in past and present, and you temper loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 方分憂於外服，來輸駿於上閑，欲助邊防，以增武備。

translations.literal: While you share my cares in an outer command, you have sent fine steeds to the imperial stables, wishing to aid frontier defense and increase military readiness.
translations.idiomatic: While you bear my cares in an outer post, you have sent fine horses to the imperial stables, wishing to strengthen the frontier and add to our military readiness.

sentences.zh: 惟盡心于體國，乃因物以見誠。

translations.literal: In devoting your heart wholly to serving the state, you have shown your sincerity through this gift.
translations.idiomatic: In giving your whole heart to the state, you have shown your sincerity through this gift.

sentences.zh: 載念懇勤，良深嘉獎。」

translations.literal: Reflecting on your earnest diligence, I commend you most warmly."
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of your earnest devotion, I commend you warmly."

sentences.zh: 五年，再任。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was reappointed.

sentences.zh: 俄召還，以疾不能入見。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled, but illness prevented him from entering audience.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled, but illness kept him from appearing at court.

sentences.zh: 上親幸其第臨視。

translations.literal: The emperor personally visited his residence to see him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went in person to his home to visit him.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年，薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，上為之震悼，賻贈甚厚，諡曰忠獻。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, the emperor was shaken with grief; funeral gifts were very generous, and the posthumous name Zhongxian was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his death arrived, the emperor was deeply shaken; funeral gifts were lavish, and he was given the posthumous name Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 永成自幼喜讀書，晚年所學益醇，每暇日引文士相與切磋，接之以禮，未嘗見驕色。

translations.literal: From youth Yong Cheng delighted in reading; in his later years his learning grew still purer. On free days he would invite literary men to study together, treating them with courtesy and never showing an arrogant air.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Cheng loved books from childhood; in later years his learning grew ever richer. On his free days he would invite literary men to study with him, treating them courteously and never showing arrogance.

sentences.zh: 自號曰「樂善居士」，有文集行於世雲。

translations.literal: He styled himself "Retired Scholar Who Delights in Goodness," and a collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He took the style "Retired Scholar Who Delights in Goodness," and a collection of his writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 夔王允升，改名永升，本名斜不出，一名鶴壽。

translations.literal: Prince of Kui Yun Sheng, who changed his name to Yong Sheng, was originally named Xiebuchu and also called Heshou.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Sheng, Prince of Kui, who took the name Yong Sheng, was born Xiebuchu and also known as Heshou.

sentences.zh: 大定十一年，封徐王，進封虞王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dading he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xu and advanced to Prince of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Dading he was made Prince of Xu and promoted to Prince of Yu.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was granted the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was given the rank of Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 明年，判吏部尚書，授山東西路按必出虎必剌猛安。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Minister of Civil Office and granted the Anbichuhu Bila meng'an on the Shandong Western Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Minister of Civil Office and granted the Anbichuhu Bila meng'an in western Shandong.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，加恩宗室，徙封隋王，除定武軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, he was favored among the imperial clan, transferred to Prince of Sui, and appointed military commissioner of Dingwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong came to the throne, he was favored among the imperial clan, reassigned as Prince of Sui, and made commissioner of the Dingwu army.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，改封曹王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingchang he was transferred to Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingchang he was reassigned as Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 久之，改封宛王。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Prince of Wan.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was reassigned as Prince of Wan.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王即位，徙今封。

translations.literal: When Prince of Wei-Shao took the throne, Yong Sheng was transferred to his present title.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei-Shao came to the throne, Yong Sheng was given his present title.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年九月，宣宗以允升年高，素羸疾，詔宮中聽扶杖。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Zhenyou, because Yun Sheng was advanced in years and chronically frail, Xuanzong ordered that he be allowed to use a staff within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Zhenyou, because Yun Sheng was old and chronically frail, Xuanzong allowed him to use a staff within the palace.

sentences.zh: 尋薨。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 既殯，燒飯，上親臨奠。

translations.literal: After the encoffining, at the burnt-offering rite the emperor came in person to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: After the encoffining, at the burnt-offering rite the emperor came in person to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：世宗保全宗室，無所不至，雖矯海陵之失，亦由天資仁厚而然也。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: Shizong preserved the imperial clan by every means — though this corrected the errors of Hailing, it also arose from a nature innately generous and mild.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist writes: Shizong spared no effort to protect the imperial clan; though this corrected Hailing's excesses, it also sprang from a nature that was generous and mild by birth.

sentences.zh: 其子永中、永蹈皆死章宗之手，其理蓋有不可詰者。

translations.literal: His sons Yong Zhong and Yong Dao both died at Zhangzong's hands — the principle behind this is perhaps beyond full inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yong Zhong and Yong Dao both died at Zhangzong's hands — the justice of it is perhaps beyond full reckoning.

sentences.zh: 章宗無後，則厥報不爽矣。

translations.literal: Zhangzong left no heir — then retribution was not slow in coming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong left no heir — and so the retribution was not long delayed.
